661-faculty-of-dental-medicine-and-oral-: Known worldwide for teaching and multidisciplinary research in dentistry, craniofacial and oral health.
661-vision: A healthy, equitable society, promoting oral health for everyone, especially underserved people.
661-mission: Develop competent, committed professionals, foster research, deliver care in hospitals and outreach, and lead in education and health policy to reduce inequalities.
661-faculty-of-dental-medicine-and-oral-: Known worldwide for teaching and multidisciplinary research.
661-health-sciences-general-information: Adds health sciences details to the University Regulations: language, immunization, immigration and facilities. Your faculty may add more.
661-clinical-facilities-for-dentistry: The Undergraduate Teaching Dental Clinic is at Place Mercantile, 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 100, where students train daily under staff guidance.
662-fees-health-sciences: Updated March 2026 and may change. See p. 44 and the Student Accounts Fee Calculator.
662-general-fees: Application: $136.08 for undergraduate programs, $190.51 for Medicine and Dentistry. Reconsideration: $40. Prepayment: Dentistry $500, Pre-Dentistry $400, Medicine $500.
662-dentistry-purchases-of-equipment-and: Equipment and supplies billed on your e-bill, estimated for 2026–2027: first year $400, second $17,000, third $4,100, fourth $2,500. Your August e-bill gives the breakdown.
662-dentistry-extra-fees: White coat about $35. Supplemental or reread exam request $45.16 each.
662-dentistry-laptops: Courseware and exams are online, so a laptop meeting minimum requirements is required.
662-dentistry-and-medicine-microscopes: A binocular microscope is provided in first and second year.
662-medicine-fees: Books, lab materials, dissection kit, stethoscope and so on: about $1,500–$2,000 over the program. White coat about $50. CMQ registration $130 at the start of first year (September 30). Police check $115 on admission.
662-medicine-extra-fees: Vaccines free at a CLSC. French Medical Workshop $385 per course, recommended, as all need working French for rotations. MCCQE $1,500, USMLE $1,600 USD (optional), CaRMS $300.
663-medicine-laptops: A laptop meeting minimum requirements for all four years.
663-nursing-fees: Books, uniform, stethoscope: about $2,500–$3,500. Graduation pins $80–$200. Name badge about $26. OIIQ about $250. Transit to sites about $100 a month. Clinical Skills Kit varies.
663-immigration-information: Non-Canadians studying six months or more need Québec and federal authorization before coming, starting with McGill's acceptance letter. Nursing students also need a co-op work permit. ISS sends a pamphlet and Handbook. Brown Building, Suite 5100.
663-student-advising: Seek out advice actively. Your records, course choices, requirements and deadlines are ultimately your responsibility.
663-your-advisor: A faculty or staff member who guides you on academic and other concerns, workload, careers and difficulties, and links you to other resources. Nursing: see your Student Handbook.
663-language-policy: Instruction is in English, but most Québec clinical placements need English and French, so build skills early.
Dentistry: working knowledge of both. Dietetics: both, with French proof for admission.
Medicine: English in Montréal, French at Campus Outaouais; working French from the start, with no alternative placements. You may be assigned a year-long clerkship in Gatineau or rural sites.

Nursing: written work in either language, French proficiency required for B.Sc.(N.) and Qualifying Year. Physical and Occupational Therapy: both needed; without French, fewer placements and possibly delayed graduation.
664-proof-of-proficiency-in-english: Not needed if English is your first language, you did Secondary V and a DCS in Québec, or studied five+ years in English.
Otherwise: TOEFL 90 iBT or 577 paper (varies), McGill Certificate of Proficiency, IELTS 6.5, MELAB 85%, or APIEL 4.
664-proof-of-proficiency-in-french: Clinical work requires French to learn safely and support patients. Essential for several Nursing degrees.
Physical and Occupational Therapy: all sites need both languages under the Charter of the French Language, so reach an appropriate level before placements.
664-vaccination-immunization-requirement: Compulsory: begin once accepted, finish well before patient contact, with proof signed by a nurse or physician. No exceptions; otherwise you're asked to withdraw. Influenza and others may be required.
D.M.D., General Practice Residency and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery applicants are tested for Hepatitis B. A positive "e" antigen or viral DNA result withdraws the offer.

Students seropositive for Hepatitis B, C, HIV or other blood-borne pathogens must tell the Dean or Director, and follow the provincial service's recommendations, which may restrict procedures and could mean withdrawing. Those who know they carry such pathogens should weigh this carefully.
With a contagious disease that risks patients, tell your supervisor; you may have to pause clinical work.

Medicine and Dentistry have further UGME policies, and Nursing its own list. Physical and Occupational Therapy need complete records and a mask fitting before the first clinical course, with a card submitted by the third clinical seminar.
665-international-dental-graduates: For graduates of non-CDAC-accredited programs: enter second year and get a D.M.D. in three years, starting in August, with places varying yearly.
To be licensed without it, use the NDEB Equivalency Process, three assessments before written and OSCE exams. For Québec, consult the Ordre des dentistes.
666-admission-requirements: A graduate of a non-accredited program, and a Québec resident, Canadian citizen or PR. ADAT between March 1, 2025 and March 10, 2026 (2023–24 also accepted). CASPer. TOEFL 90 or IELTS 6.5 if needed.

French at B2 before the deadline, or B1 plus enrolment in B2 courses completed before Year 3; otherwise studies halt. Black and Indigenous pathway exemptions don't apply. Immunization required. Apply by March 1.
666-students-enrolled-in-a-graduate-prog: You can't be in another program at once. Apply when nearly finished: thesis submitted by July 31, confirmed by November 15; doctoral students show a successful defence by July 31, or the offer is withdrawn.
666-licensure-by-the-order-of-dentists: A degree alone doesn't let you practise. Follow local dental laws, and register with the licensing body when you begin.
666-national-dental-examining-board-of-c: Canadian graduates need an NDEB certificate, normally by exam in final year. 80 Elgin St., 2nd Floor, Ottawa.
666-province-of-quebec: An NDEB certificate plus the French requirement (p. 70). Ordre des Dentistes: 800 René-Lévesque Blvd. W., Suite 1640.
666-dental-regulatory-authorities-in-oth: Contact these bodies about each province's rules.
667-alberta: Alberta Dental Association, 8230 105th St., Suite 101, Edmonton.
667-british-columbia: College of Dental Surgeons of BC, 1765 West 8th Ave., Suite 500, Vancouver.
667-manitoba: Manitoba Dental Association, 1735 Corydon Ave., Suite 202, Winnipeg.
667-new-brunswick: New Brunswick Dental Society, 570 Queen St., Suite 504, Fredericton.
667-newfoundland-and-labrador: Newfoundland and Labrador Dental Board, 49–55 Elizabeth Ave., Suite 204, St. John's.
667-nova-scotia: Provincial Dental Board of Nova Scotia, 210 Waterfront Dr., Suite 103, Bedford.
667-ontario: Royal College of Dental Surgeons of Ontario, 6 Crescent Rd., Toronto.
667-prince-edward-island: Dental Association of PEI, 184 Belvedere Ave., Charlottetown.
667-saskatchewan: College of Dental Surgeons of Saskatchewan, 201 First Ave. S., Unit 1202, Saskatoon.
667-national-board-of-dental-examiners-u: American Dental Association, 211 East Chicago Ave., Chicago, and the state's licensing board.
667-basic-cardiac-life-support: By July 31 of your entry year, show CPR level C or C+ and AED training, kept valid throughout, from Heart and Stroke, Red Cross, St. John Ambulance or the American Heart Association. Upload to your checklist.
667-compulsory-immunization-program: Submit the form by July 31 of your entry year through the Wellness Hub portal; you consent to the Admissions Office sharing your health details for verification. You may need a meeting.
668-instruments: Everyone buys a complete McGill Instrument Kit (p. 947).
668-new-students: Register in Minerva by August 14 and check your transcript. Orientation week is mandatory, or your application may be cancelled. Details come in June.
668-returning-students: You get a list of Fall, Winter and Summer courses to register for in Minerva.
668-dental-officer-training-plan: The Canadian Forces pays tuition, instruments, supplies and books with a second lieutenant's rank and salary, in return for short service after graduating, with summer officer training. Meet Forces standards and be accepted into a professional year. 1420 Sainte-Catherine St. W.
668-entrance-scholarships-for-the-facult: A few each year, on merit, usually with no application. See the Financial Aid site.
668-mccall-macbain-scholarships: A full scholarship and enrichment program for professional or master's study at McGill.
668-dr-yu-ming-lam-scholarship: Since 1999, for high achievers entering the four-year program. Renewable with standing.
668-ping-kwan-lau-scholarship: Since 1998, for high achievers entering the program, preferring international students. Renewable.
668-phyllis-butterworth-major-entrance-s: For high achievers, preferring students from the UK. Renewable.
668-dr-harry-rosen-entrance-scholarship-: Since 2004, for an outstanding student entering the program. Renewable.
669-dr-leo-paul-ramsay-major-entrance-sc: Since 2023, for academic excellence at entry, preferring Québec students with community leadership.
669-award-for-indigenous-undergraduate-s: OKÒN:RA Award for full-time Indigenous students in any undergraduate degree, including D.M.D. Application needed.
669-financial-aid-for-the-faculty-of-den: Start with government aid, and accept the maximum, plus a professional line of credit. Then apply in Minerva and meet a counsellor for low-interest loans and limited bursaries. Suite 3200, Brown Building.
669-in-course-scholarships-for-the-facul: For high-standing full-time students. Advanced Standing students must meet each prize's exact criteria.
669-dr-ernest-r-ambrose-scholarship-in-d: Since 2001, for common sense, compassion and excellence in restorative dentistry, preferring those entering fourth year.
669-dr-janet-griffin-merth-scholarship-i: Since 2002, for academic achievement after at least one year, preferring students from BC.
669-dr-james-e-g-harrison-scholarship-in: Since 2001, for commitment to ethical practice, preferring those entering third or fourth year.
669-dr-howard-s-katz-scholarship-in-dent: Since 2001, for academic achievement after at least one year.
670-dr-william-boroff-scholarship-in-den: Since 2004, for character, perseverance and sportsmanship, preferring those entering fourth year.
670-dr-harry-rosen-scholarship-in-dentis: Since 2004, for high standing after at least one year, preferring those entering fourth year.
670-carol-david-scholarship: Since 2019, for high standing and pre-clinical skills after two years. Renewable.
670-rena-and-mervyn-gornitsky-scholarshi: Since 2005, for performance and initiative in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, preferring those entering fourth year.
670-dr-robert-axelrad-award: Since 2022, for one or two students showing warmth and empathy with patients.
670-dr-stanley-s-blum-award: Since 2023, at the White Coat Ceremony, for interest and excellence in restorative dentistry.
670-medals-and-prizes-in-the-faculty-of-: By a policy begun by the Dental Students' Society, only prizes listed here appear on records.
670-dr-m-donigan-award: Highest standing in Physicianship and Dentistry Apprenticeship units.
670-dr-maxwell-and-betty-l-goldenberg-pr: Highest in the practical clinical part of Cycle Two, second year.
670-dr-k-i-melville-award: Highest in second-year Foundations of Dentistry.
670-pierre-fauchard-academy-prize: The junior CDA Student Governor, for leadership.
671-dr-lyman-e-francis-prize: Highest in third-year Pharmacology, Oral Pathology, Medicine and Radiology.
671-dr-philip-j-and-mrs-stella-gitnick-p: Since 2009, highest in Periodontology on entering fourth year.
671-dr-leanore-k-feine-prize: Commitment to the local community's oral health.
671-canadian-dental-association-student-: A graduating CDA member with outstanding leadership, scholarship, character and humanity.
671-dr-j-k-carver-award: Second-highest overall across four years, from the Ordre des Dentistes.
671-dr-soo-kim-lan-prize-in-dentistry: Since 2000, an outstanding graduate entering a residency or postgraduate program.
671-dr-james-mccutcheon-medal: A graduate with outstanding leadership, scholarship and professional achievement.
671-mcgill-alumnae-society-prize: Excellence and high standing at graduation, preferring women.
671-prix-micheline-blain-acdq: A graduate who best served colleagues, from the Québec Dental Surgeons Association.
671-dr-a-gerald-racey-prize: Excellence in the OSCE of the final oral and maxillofacial exam.
671-dr-a-w-thornton-medal: Highest overall across four years, from the Montreal Dental Club.
671-prix-dexcellence-jean-robert-vincent: Highest in Geriatric Dentistry, from the Québec Association for Special Care Dentistry.
671-dr-marvin-and-mandy-werbitt-award-in: Since 2008, a graduate with initiative and strong standing in Periodontology.
672-evaluation-and-promotion-in-dentistr: The Student Promotion Committee decides on promotion and graduation. Rules may change, generally not mid-year. See the Professionalism Standard, Absences and Leaves Policy, Ethical Behaviour guidelines and Promotion Guidelines.
672-about-dentistry: A dynamic D.M.D. curriculum aimed at sound judgment and evidence-based care with social justice, linking oral and general health, and preparing leaders to tackle disparities.
672-admissions-undergraduate-program: Applications open September 1 the year before, with a non-refundable fee. Any field of study is welcome. The Faculty seeks socially aware, community-minded people with listening, empathy and compassion.
672-application-deadlines-undergraduate-: Four-year D.M.D.: apply November 1, documents November 3. Dent-P: apply March 1, documents March 3. Advanced Standing: apply March 1, documents March 3.
Accepting requires a CAD $500 deposit against tuition.
672-deferred-admission: Exceptionally one year, at the Committee's discretion, after an offer. Write to the Chair of Admissions by July 15, in two pages at most with documents, plus a non-refundable $500. Not for Dent-P or Advanced Standing.
673-extenuating-circumstances: Serious medical or personal difficulties affecting your grades can be claimed on your application.
673-students-enrolled-in-a-graduate-prog: No concurrent programs, so apply in your final year. Thesis submitted and confirmed by July 31 of your entry year, or the offer is withdrawn.
673-four-year-undergraduate-dental-progr: 16 months of Fundamentals of Medicine and Dentistry with Medicine, seven months of preclinical training, then two clinical years, with rotations at Montreal General, Montreal Children's, the Jim Lund Clinic at Welcome Hall Mission, and the Alan Edwards Pain Unit.
673-requirements: A full-time 120-credit bachelor's in any field by July 31 of entry, or 90 credits with a pre-university DEC. A second degree counts with 45 new graded credits by November 1 and 15 more by July 31. A marked decline can cost the offer. No narrative transcripts.
673-basic-science-requirements: With labs: 6 credits Biology, 6 General or Physical Chemistry, 3 Organic Chemistry, 6 Physics (3 of Calculus can count for half). All by May 31 of applying, with four of seven done by November 1. Graded, not P/F (except Winter 2020). A-Levels, French Baccalaureate, IB HL and AP may be accepted.
Cell biology, physiology, statistics and genetics are strongly recommended.
673-casper-test-computer-based-assessmen: Mandatory before the deadline: 12 sections of video and written scenarios, assessing personal skills, each scored by a different rater. No studying needed; do the practice test. You need a webcam computer. Valid one cycle.
674-dental-aptitude-test-dat: Removed for Fall 2025 entry, with future use under review.
674-french-language-requirements: B2 by the start of Clinical Practice in third year.
674-dentistry-preparatory-qualifying-yea: A year in the Faculty of Science to adapt to university, then the D.M.D. Keep CGPA 3.5 to continue.
674-requirements: Québec residents in the final year of CEGEP Sciences, not university students or from outside Québec. At least six courses each semester. Three-year Science and Science-IB, and Arts and Science (700.A0) with the competencies, can qualify. Collège Marie de France and Stanislas qualify under conditions.
674-basic-science-requirements: Biology NYA and NYB, Chemistry NYA, NYB and Organic I, Math NYA–NYC, Physics NYA–NYC. 700.A0 and IB-DEC have their own equivalents, with preference for closer matches.
674-applicants-not-admissible-to-the-den: DEC taking over two years, those who already have a DEC or have registered in a degree, and LCC IB or Stanstead Grade 12.
Exceptions: remedial entry, transfer into Science within three years, Sport-études with a form, and Dental Hygiene DEC followed by Science within five. You may still apply to the four-year D.M.D.
675-dentistry-four-year-program-d-m-d-22: Fundamentals with Medicine, preclinical training, then two clinical years with hospital rotations and the McGill Pain Centre.
675-dental-preparatory-dent-p-b-sc-30-cr: A preparatory Science year, then the D.M.D., with CGPA 3.5.
675-program-description: Simulation and clinical training, with Fundamentals taught with Medicine and hospital rotations.
677-program-description: 30 credits in Science (18 required, 12 humanities electives), then four years. Promotion needs CGPA 3.5, B or higher in each required course, and passes in complementaries. Otherwise transfer to a B.Sc. and reapply later.
678-about-general-practice-residency-gpr: One year of advanced general dentistry across specialties, with oral sedation, BLS and ACLS. Canada's largest, with 23 residents, at Montreal General, Montreal Children's and Jewish General.
678-admissions-requirements: CDA or ADA-approved graduates or final-year students, with the degree by registration. Based on standing and interviews. Apply to the ODQ for a temporary permit. Québec graduates must pass ODQ's exam. No narrative transcripts.
678-french-language-requirement: Québec graduates must show French before a permit, with no temporary permit, usually by OQLF exam unless schooled in French.
Others may get a permit for up to a year, renewable three times, passing the OQLF exam in time.
678-application-procedures: Online, not through the undergraduate portal, opening each fall. Official transcripts, three references (your Dean and two dental professors), and a personal statement, plus another if applying to Montreal Children's. Put your McGill ID on everything.
679-program-description: Advanced general practice training, with sedation, BLS and ACLS, from accredited Canadian or U.S. schools and eligible for Québec licensure. Those not schooled in Québec must meet OQLF's French requirement first.
680-about-oral-and-maxillofacial-surgery: Oral Surgery Internship, sponsored 2-year internship and 4-year program, Integrated O.M.F.S. & M.D.,C.M. residency, and an ad hoc Fellowship in Maxillofacial Oncology and Microvascular Reconstruction.
680-oral-surgery-internship-cert-52-cred: One year for Canadians or PRs from accredited North American schools, working with residents. Two years, unfunded, only for graduates of programs with a sponsorship agreement.
680-sponsored-2-year-internship-and-4-ye: Sponsor-funded, only for graduates of programs with a sponsorship agreement.
680-oral-and-maxillofacial-surgery-integ: Six years, giving an M.D.,C.M. and a Certificate, accredited by CDAC, LCME and CACMS.
680-admissions-requirements: See Find your program, or contact the Division.
680-application-procedures: Online only: unofficial transcripts (McGill can demand official ones and rescind offers), three references, CV, personal statement, and possibly the National Board Comprehensive Basic Science Exam.
680-location: Montreal General Hospital, 1650 Cedar Ave., Room B3.119.
674-casper-test-computer-based-assessmen: CASPer required; see the Dent-P Requirements page.
